_meta.purpose: Drug-drug interaction rules, duplicate-therapy groups and dose limits for the educational medication safety engine.
_meta.review_status: Draft clinical content summarised from commonly cited references and FDA labeling. Must be reviewed by pharmacy/clinical faculty before being used for grading.
_meta.rule_format: Each side ('a', 'b') is a list of tokens. A token is either a drug class from formulary.json or an exact drug name. A rule fires for two different drugs when one matches side a and the other matches side b. 'all_of' rules need distinct drugs matching every group. When several rules match the same pair, only the highest severity is reported (drug-specific wins ties).

interactions.title: Dual renin-angiotensin system blockade
interactions.description: Combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB adds little benefit and increases the risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid the combination. Choose one agent unless a specialist has directed otherwise.

interactions.title: Hyperkalemia risk
interactions.description: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce potassium excretion. Adding a potassium-sparing diuretic or a potassium supplement can cause dangerous hyperkalemia.
interactions.recommendation: Check serum potassium and renal function within 1-2 weeks and periodically afterward, or choose an alternative.

interactions.title: Hyperkalemia risk
interactions.description: A potassium-sparing diuretic combined with a potassium supplement can raise serum potassium to dangerous levels.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid routine co-prescribing. If used together, monitor potassium closely.

interactions.title: Reduced antihypertensive effect and kidney injury risk
interactions.description: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandins, which can blunt the blood pressure effect of ACE inhibitors and ARBs and increase the risk of kidney injury.
interactions.recommendation: Prefer acetaminophen for pain where appropriate. If an NSAID is needed, use the lowest dose for the shortest time and monitor blood pressure and creatinine.

interactions.title: 'Triple whammy' acute kidney injury risk
interactions.description: An ACE inhibitor or ARB, a diuretic and an NSAID taken together markedly raise the risk of acute kidney injury.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid the three-drug combination. Stop or replace the NSAID and monitor renal function.

interactions.title: Increased bleeding risk
interactions.description: NSAIDs impair platelet function and irritate the gastric mucosa, which substantially raises the risk of serious bleeding in anticoagulated patients.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with anticoagulants. Use acetaminophen for analgesia where appropriate.

interactions.title: Increased bleeding risk
interactions.description: Combining an anticoagulant with an antiplatelet agent increases the risk of major bleeding.
interactions.recommendation: Use only when there is a clear indication, at the lowest effective duration, and monitor for bleeding.

interactions.title: Increased GI bleeding risk
interactions.description: NSAIDs combined with antiplatelet agents raise the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. Ibuprofen can also interfere with the antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid when possible. Consider gastroprotection and counsel the patient on bleeding signs.

interactions.title: Increased bleeding risk
interactions.description: SSRIs and SNRIs impair platelet aggregation and add to the bleeding risk of anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for bleeding and consider gastroprotection.

interactions.title: Increased GI ulcer and bleeding risk
interactions.description: NSAIDs combined with corticosteroids increase the risk of peptic ulcer disease and gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.recommendation: Use the lowest effective doses for the shortest time and consider a proton pump inhibitor.

interactions.title: Increased GI bleeding risk
interactions.description: SSRIs and SNRIs combined with NSAIDs increase the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.recommendation: Prefer acetaminophen where appropriate. Consider gastroprotection if the combination is needed.

interactions.title: Large change in warfarin effect (INR)
interactions.description: These agents substantially change warfarin metabolism or protein binding. Most raise the INR and bleeding risk; strong enzyme inducers lower the INR and can cause loss of anticoagulation.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor the INR closely when starting, stopping or changing the interacting drug, and adjust the warfarin dose accordingly.

interactions.title: Possible change in warfarin effect (INR)
interactions.description: These agents can raise or alter the INR in patients taking warfarin.
interactions.recommendation: Check the INR within a few days of starting or stopping the interacting drug.

interactions.title: Reduced anticoagulant effect
interactions.description: Strong enzyme inducers lower direct oral anticoagulant levels and may cause loss of stroke or clot protection.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid the combination or choose an alternative anticoagulant.

interactions.title: Serotonin syndrome / hypertensive crisis
interactions.description: MAO inhibitors combined with serotonergic drugs or bupropion can cause life-threatening serotonin syndrome or hypertensive crisis.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine. A washout period is required between an MAOI and any serotonergic agent.

interactions.title: Serotonin syndrome and seizure risk
interactions.description: Tramadol combined with SSRIs, SNRIs or tricyclics increases the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid when possible. Choose a different analgesic or monitor closely for serotonin toxicity.

interactions.title: Serotonin syndrome risk
interactions.description: Combining multiple serotonergic drugs can lead to serotonin syndrome (agitation, tremor, hyperthermia, tachycardia).
interactions.recommendation: Use the lowest effective doses and counsel the patient on warning signs.

interactions.title: Severe hypotension
interactions.description: PDE5 inhibitors combined with nitrates can cause profound, life-threatening hypotension. The labeling lists the combination as contraindicated.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine. Nitrates must not be given within the labeled window after a PDE5 inhibitor.

interactions.title: Additive hypotension
interactions.description: PDE5 inhibitors and alpha-blockers both lower blood pressure and can cause symptomatic hypotension.
interactions.recommendation: Start at the lowest dose and separate dosing as directed in the labeling.

interactions.title: Profound sedation and respiratory depression
interactions.description: Concurrent opioids and benzodiazepines carry an FDA boxed warning for profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid when possible. If both are needed, use the lowest doses and shortest duration and monitor closely.

interactions.title: Respiratory depression
interactions.description: Gabapentinoids combined with opioids increase the risk of respiratory depression and sedation.
interactions.recommendation: Use the lowest effective doses and monitor respiratory status, especially in older adults and patients with lung disease.

interactions.title: Additive sedation
interactions.description: Combining multiple CNS depressants increases drowsiness, impaired coordination and fall risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use the lowest effective doses and counsel the patient about driving and alcohol.

interactions.title: Additive QT prolongation
interactions.description: Combining QT-prolonging drugs increases the risk of torsades de pointes, a life-threatening arrhythmia.
interactions.recommendation: Obtain a baseline ECG, correct potassium and magnesium, and consider alternatives.

interactions.title: Bradycardia and AV block
interactions.description: Beta-blockers combined with diltiazem or verapamil can cause severe bradycardia, AV block and heart failure.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid or use with close monitoring of heart rate, blood pressure and ECG.

interactions.title: Digoxin toxicity
interactions.description: Amiodarone raises digoxin levels, increasing the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce the digoxin dose and monitor digoxin levels and ECG.

interactions.title: Bradycardia and increased digoxin effect
interactions.description: Beta-blockers, diltiazem and verapamil add to the AV-nodal slowing of digoxin, and verapamil and diltiazem can raise digoxin levels.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor heart rate, ECG and digoxin levels.

interactions.title: Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity
interactions.description: Loop and thiazide diuretics can lower potassium and magnesium, which increases the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor electrolytes and digoxin levels.

interactions.title: Increased digoxin levels
interactions.description: Macrolide antibiotics, particularly clarithromycin, can raise digoxin levels and cause toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for digoxin toxicity and consider checking levels.

interactions.title: Additive bradycardia
interactions.description: Amiodarone combined with beta-blockers can cause symptomatic bradycardia and AV block.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor heart rate and ECG.

interactions.title: Rebound hypertension and bradycardia
interactions.description: Beta-blockers can worsen rebound hypertension if clonidine is stopped abruptly and add to bradycardia.
interactions.recommendation: Taper clonidine gradually and stop the beta-blocker first if both are being discontinued.

interactions.title: Severe hypoglycemia risk
interactions.description: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim can increase the hypoglycemic effect of sulfonylureas.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose closely or choose a different antibiotic.

interactions.title: Blood glucose disturbance
interactions.description: Fluoroquinolones can cause both hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia in patients taking antidiabetic drugs.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose and counsel the patient on hypoglycemia symptoms.

interactions.title: Masked hypoglycemia symptoms
interactions.description: Beta-blockers can hide the warning signs of hypoglycemia such as tremor and palpitations and may prolong recovery.
interactions.recommendation: Counsel the patient to monitor glucose regularly. Sweating may remain as a warning sign.

interactions.title: Reduced glycemic control
interactions.description: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose and can offset the effect of antidiabetic medications.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose and adjust the antidiabetic regimen while the steroid is used.

interactions.title: Fluid retention and heart failure risk
interactions.description: Pioglitazone combined with insulin increases the risk of edema and congestive heart failure.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor weight and signs of fluid overload.

interactions.title: Volume depletion
interactions.description: SGLT2 inhibitors have a diuretic effect that adds to loop diuretics and can cause dehydration and hypotension.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor volume status and renal function and consider reducing the diuretic dose.

interactions.title: Lithium toxicity
interactions.description: NSAIDs and thiazide diuretics reduce renal lithium clearance and can raise lithium levels into the toxic range.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid the combination. If it is unavoidable, monitor lithium levels closely.

interactions.title: Increased lithium levels
interactions.description: ACE inhibitors and ARBs can reduce lithium clearance and raise lithium levels.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor lithium levels and renal function.

interactions.title: Reduced clopidogrel effectiveness
interactions.description: Omeprazole and esomeprazole inhibit CYP2C19, which activates clopidogrel. The FDA label advises avoiding the combination because antiplatelet effect is reduced.
interactions.recommendation: Use a PPI with less CYP2C19 inhibition, such as pantoprazole, if acid suppression is needed.

interactions.title: Reduced analgesic effect
interactions.description: CYP2D6 inhibitors block conversion of tramadol to its active metabolite, reducing pain relief while serotonergic effects persist.
interactions.recommendation: Consider a non-CYP2D6-dependent analgesic.

interactions.title: Increased drug levels (CYP2D6 inhibition)
interactions.description: CYP2D6 inhibitors can raise levels of CYP2D6 substrates such as metoprolol and amitriptyline, increasing bradycardia, hypotension or anticholinergic effects.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure, and consider a dose reduction.

interactions.title: Reduced levothyroxine absorption
interactions.description: Calcium and iron bind levothyroxine in the gut and reduce its absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 4 hours and recheck TSH if the regimen changes.

interactions.title: Reduced antibiotic absorption
interactions.description: Calcium and iron chelate fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines, lowering antibiotic levels and risking treatment failure.
interactions.recommendation: Give the antibiotic at least 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after the supplement, per product labeling.

interactions.title: Increased tendon rupture risk
interactions.description: Fluoroquinolones carry a boxed warning for tendon rupture, and the risk rises further with corticosteroids, especially in older adults.
interactions.recommendation: Consider an alternative antibiotic and counsel the patient to stop and report tendon pain.

interactions.title: Reduced contraceptive effectiveness
interactions.description: Strong enzyme inducers such as rifampin, carbamazepine and phenytoin speed hormone metabolism and can cause contraceptive failure.
interactions.recommendation: Use an alternative or additional non-hormonal method of contraception.

interactions.title: Possible reduced contraceptive effectiveness
interactions.description: Evidence that non-rifamycin antibiotics reduce contraceptive effectiveness is limited, but it is commonly raised in clinical practice and patient counseling.
interactions.recommendation: Counsel the patient about the uncertainty and about backup contraception per local policy. Vomiting or diarrhea can also reduce absorption.

interactions.title: Increased statin levels (myopathy risk)
interactions.description: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin raise levels of several statins and increase the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
interactions.recommendation: Temporarily hold the statin during the antibiotic course or choose a non-interacting agent.

interactions.title: Rhabdomyolysis risk
interactions.description: Simvastatin is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin because of the risk of rhabdomyolysis.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine. Hold simvastatin during clarithromycin or use an alternative antibiotic.

interactions.title: Simvastatin dose limit with amiodarone
interactions.description: Amiodarone raises simvastatin exposure. The labeling limits the simvastatin dose to 20 mg daily.
interactions.recommendation: Do not exceed simvastatin 20 mg daily or choose a different statin.

interactions.title: Simvastatin dose limit with diltiazem or verapamil
interactions.description: Diltiazem and verapamil raise simvastatin exposure. The labeling recommends dose limits to reduce myopathy risk.
interactions.recommendation: Limit the simvastatin dose per labeling or choose a different statin.

interactions.title: Colchicine toxicity
interactions.description: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors markedly raise colchicine levels and can cause fatal toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce the colchicine dose per labeling or avoid the combination, especially in renal impairment.

interactions.title: Additive extrapyramidal effects
interactions.description: Metoclopramide combined with antipsychotics increases the risk of extrapyramidal symptoms and neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid the combination. Choose a different antiemetic.
